fullPassage: For astronauts in space, the force of gravity is weaker than it is on Earth. Because of this, astronauts sometimes develop symptoms of "space sickness," such as headaches, nausea, and vomiting. Space sickness is related to the small organs deep inside our ears that detect information about the movement of the body. They send this information to the brain, and the brain uses this information to keep the body balanced. In the low gravity of space, the information sent by those organs changes. According to scientists, this difference confuses the brain and results in the symptoms associated with space sickness. Luckily, space sickness does not last very long. After a few days, the brain adapts to the lower gravity of the astronauts' environment, and the symptoms go away. However, in some cases, astronauts can experience "gravity sickness," which has symptoms that are similar to those of space sickness, when they return to Earth.
